question: What did they teach about same-sex acts?

answers.label: Same-sex acts are sinful, against nature

overview.text: The earliest writings forbid the pederasty common in Greek culture ("you shall not corrupt boys") and repeat Paul's lists.
Later writers argued from nature and from Romans 1: Clement, Chrysostom and Augustine all call such acts "against nature". No early writer approves them.

quotes.author: Didache
quotes.english: You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not corrupt boys; you shall not commit sexual sin.
quotes.original: οὐ φονεύσεις, οὐ μοιχεύσεις, οὐ παιδοφθορήσεις, οὐ πορνεύσεις
quotes.context: "Corrupt boys" (paidophthoria) names the pederasty common in Greek culture. Barnabas 19.4 repeats it.

quotes.author: Polycarp of Smyrna
quotes.english: Neither the sexually immoral, nor the effeminate, nor men who lie with men will inherit the kingdom of God (1 Corinthians 6:9–10), nor those who do perverse things.
quotes.original: οὔτε πόρνοι οὔτε μαλακοὶ οὔτε ἀρσενοκοῖται βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομήσουσιν, οὔτε οἱ ποιοῦντες τὰ ἄτοπα.
quotes.context: Polycarp quotes Paul's list to the young men of Philippi.

quotes.author: Justin Martyr
quotes.english: And just as the ancients are said to have kept herds of oxen or goats or sheep or grazing horses, so now children too are kept only for shameful use; and likewise a multitude of females and of hermaphrodites and of doers of unspeakable things stands ready in every nation for this pollution.
quotes.original: καὶ ὃν τρόπον λέγονται οἱ παλαιοὶ ἀγέλας βοῶν ἢ αἰγῶν ἢ προβάτων τρέφειν ἢ ἵππων φορβάδων, οὕτως νῦν καὶ παῖδας εἰς τὸ αἰσχρῶς χρῆσθαι μόνον· καὶ ὁμοίως θηλειῶν καὶ ἀνδρογύνων καὶ ἀῤῥητοποιῶν πλῆθος κατὰ πᾶν ἔθνος ἐπὶ τούτου τοῦ ἄγους ἕστηκε.
quotes.context: Justin is denouncing the exposure of infants, a pagan practice, because exposed children are raised for prostitution. He calls the trade a pollution (ἄγος) and contrasts it with the Christian teaching that exposing children is wicked.

quotes.author: Athenagoras
quotes.english: For they have set up a market of prostitution and made unlawful resorts for the young for every shameful pleasure, not sparing even males, males working the dreadful things with males, and in every way outraging the bodies that are more modest and beautiful, dishonouring the fair work of God.
quotes.original: Οἱ γὰρ ἀγορὰν στήσαντες πορνείας καὶ καταγωγὰς ἀθέσμους πεποιημένοι τοῖς νέοις πάσης αἰσχρᾶς ἡδονῆς καὶ μηδὲ τῶν ἀρσένων φειδόμενοι, ἄρσενες ἐν ἄρσεσι τὰ δεινὰ κατεργαζόμενοι
quotes.context: Athenagoras turns the pagans' slanders back on their authors: adulterers and pederasts, he says, revile Christians, who live as eunuchs and in single marriage.

quotes.author: Clement of Alexandria
quotes.english: Seed, the substance that begins generation, must not be outraged, since it has the principles of nature sown in it; and to bring shame on the natural principles by turning them unreasonably to unnatural ways is utterly godless.
quotes.original: οὐδὲ καθυβριστέον τὸ σπέρμα, ἀρχηγὸν γενέσεως οὐσίαν, συνεσπαρμένους ἔχουσαν τῆς φύσεως τοὺς λογισμούς· τοὺς δὲ κατὰ φύσιν λογισμοὺς ἀλόγως εἰς τοὺς παρὰ φύσιν καταισχύνειν πόρους ἄθεον κομιδῇ.
quotes.context: Clement's argument from nature, close to the Stoics, covers all non-procreative acts.

quotes.author: John Chrysostom
quotes.english: What women who prostitute themselves suffer, these suffer too, or rather something more wretched. For with them, even if the union is unlawful, it is according to nature; but this is both unlawful and against nature.
quotes.original: Ἃ γὰρ αἱ πορνευόμεναι πάσχουσι γυναῖκες, ταῦτα καὶ οὗτοι· μᾶλλον δὲ ἐκείνων ἀθλιώτερα. Ταῖς μὲν γὰρ εἰ καὶ παράνομος, ἀλλὰ κατὰ φύσιν ἡ μίξις· αὕτη δὲ καὶ παράνομος, καὶ παρὰ φύσιν.
quotes.context: Chrysostom notes that Greek law and philosophers had tolerated such relations.

quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo
quotes.english: So the shameful acts that are against nature, such as those of the Sodomites, are everywhere and always to be detested and punished. Even if all nations did them, they would all be held guilty of the same crime by God's law, which did not make human beings to use one another in this way.
quotes.original: itaque flagitia, quae sunt contra naturam, ubique ac semper detestanda atque punienda sunt, qualia Sodomitarum fuerunt. quae si omnes gentes facerent, eodem criminis diuina lege tenerentur, quae non sic fecit homines, ut hoc se uterentur modo.
quotes.context: Augustine contrasts acts wrong by custom with acts wrong everywhere.

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
